decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Existing elevation plan, 3595/7_Sept26Existing floor plan, 3595/9_Sept26Proposed floor plan, 3595/8_Sept26Proposed section plan, 3595/9_Nov26Block Plan, 23.09.26Location Plan, ref: 516233Highway safety impact proforma Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning

Notwithstanding the cycle parking arrangement shown on the approved plans, prior to first occupation of the development, revised details demonstrating the provision of five secure, covered and independently accessible long-stay cycle parking spaces shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority with the following criteria:-	Provision of a minimum of 5no.of long stay cycle parking spaces, one per HMO bedroom -	In an accessible location. The access route to the cycle parking enclosures should be a minimum of 1.2 metres wide to enable the bike to enter the store. It should be step free and involve no more than two doors or gates, excluding the store door, which must also have a minimum opening width of 1.2 metres.-	Long stay must be secured with a British Standard mortice lock or access fob.-	Long stay must be fully enclosed with four walls and a roof.The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details. Reason: The Council's Climate Action and Transport Policies seek to increase the use of active and sustainable transport modes. This means that access to bicycle parking should be easy and secure to remove potential barriers to cycling.

Prior to the occupation of the proposed development, details of refuse and waste storage and recycling facilities within the curtilage of the application site as required by the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and the facilities shall be retained permanently thereafter.Reason: To safeguard the amenity of the occupiers of adjoining premises; protect the general environment; prevent any obstruction to pedestrian movement and to ensure that there are adequate facilities for the storage and recycling of recoverable materials.

No independent cooking or laundry facilities, including hot plates, shall be installed in any of the respective bedrooms of the development hereby permitted and the communal kitchen, dining and living room shall be retained in perpetuity. Reason: To accord with the stipulations of definition as a House of Multiple Occupation and to safeguard the residential character of the surrounding area.

The use of the property as a House in Multiple Occupation hereby approved shall be occupied by a maximum of 5 people at any one time and shall not be subdivided or occupied as self-contained units. Reason: To accord with the stipulations of definition as a House of Multiple Occupation and to safeguard the residential character of the surrounding area.
